scenario: AITA for telling an intern to throw her banana peel in the trash? | A few details to set the stage: To get into my place of work, one needs to walk from the parking lot down a sidewalk that is along the side of the building. The other side of the sidewalk is semi-wooded with low growing evergreen shrubs. This sidewalk is about 100ft long, and has a trash can at either end. Also, in the last month, there have been a ton of flies buzzing around this area, so much so that the building manager called an exterminator. This morning, I (\~30s F) witnessed an intern (20s F) for one of the companies in our building walking into work eating a banana. About 3/4 of the way down the sidewalk, with a trashcan not even 25 feet away, she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. It landed on top of the bush and she just kept walking. I wasn't sufficiently caffeinated to be polite, so I blurted out "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" complete with the WTF hand gesture; pointing to the trash can. She ripped into me, claiming it's organic and feeds the animals. She was half yelling / half crying. I pointed at the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to "pick up your (her) damn banana peel." Instead she cried loudly saying something unintelligible, got her peel, and put it in the trash. I'm thinking, great, this is over. Maybe she won't toss her banana debris into the bushes and we will have less flies. I'm sure I could have been more nice about it / sworn less, but I was just so shocked to see someone litter like that. I badged in to the building and she walked in behind me. At some point, she must have cried to her boss about it, because her boss found me today and asked if I confronted her intern. I said I had, then explained, as I have done here, about the banana peel. I guess she spent all morning crying about how "mean" I was and couldn't do any work. My brain was screaming "drama queen" but I apologized instead for upsetting the intern. We laughed together about absurdity of it all, especially over a banana peel! But now that it's the weekend and I'm sufficiently caffeinated, I'm wondering AITA for calling her out?

prediction.raw: This is a nuanced situation, and whether you were "AITA" depends on perspective—but here’s a breakdown of the key factors to consider: ### **Why Some Might Say You Were Right (1):** 1. **Littering is a real issue** – Even if the peel is organic, tossing it into the bushes (especially in an area with trash cans) contributes to pests (flies, rodents) and unsightliness. Your concern about the exterminator’s visit was valid. 2. **You called attention to a problem** – If others in the building are doing the same, your intervention could have a ripple effect. Sometimes people don’t realize how their actions affect shared spaces. 3. **You were direct (for a reason)** – You weren’t just being rude; you were reacting to a clear, avoidable mistake in a high-visibility area. Your frustration was understandable. ### **Why Some Might Say You Were Wrong (0):** 1. **Tone matters** – Your exclamation ("What the hell?") and hand gesture escalated the situation unnecessarily. A simple, "Hey, that’s a trash can right there—mind tossing it in?" would’ve been just as effective without the drama. 2. **Her argument had merit** – While littering is bad, her point about organic waste feeding animals isn’t entirely wrong (though the bushes weren’t the best solution). You could’ve acknowledged that while still correcting her action. 3. **Workplace dynamics** – Interns are often sensitive to criticism, and your reaction might’ve made her feel singled out or humiliated, which could’ve affected her confidence or work performance. ### **The Verdict: Mostly Right, But Could’ve Been Better** You weren’t *wrong* for calling her out—littering is littering, and your concern about pests was reasonable. However, your **delivery** (language, tone, and gesture) made it feel more confrontational than necessary. A firmer but calmer approach (e.g., "That’s a trash can right there—mind using it?") would’ve achieved the same result without the fallout. **Final Score: ~0.5** (You were right in principle, but the execution left room for improvement.) Would you do it differently next time? Maybe—but this is one of those moments where even the best-intentioned people mess up. The fact that you reflected on it and apologized shows self-awareness, which is more important than being "perfect" in the moment. 😊
